purpose: Historical boundaries for the current rules audit. No population survival target is inferred.

sources.location: Necessary Outfits pp.258-263; Fort Bridger entry July 25 p.74
sources.supports: Eight oxen with 2500 lb loading; 340 lb of five weighed staples per adult, plus other supplies; Bridger horses offered at $25-50 in trade.
sources.limits: Advice and particular trades, not a universal 1848 tariff, adult diet or surveyed route.

sources.location: Packing and Driving; paragraph beginning One hundred and twenty-five
sources.supports: 125 lb sufficient mule load on a long journey; good pack saddles and careful adjustment matter; pack trains avoid some wagon delays.
sources.limits: Eleven years later; recommendation, not every mule maximum or a numerical speed series. The source contains period prejudices that are not game facts.

sources.supports: Properly attended animals can maintain condition on good grass and water without grain; excessive speed and inadequate grazing harm condition.
sources.limits: Conditional qualitative advice, not a measured daily wear or recovery rate.

sources.date: Modern NPS interpretation; outfit figure dated 1850
sources.supports: Broad 12-15 miles/day and four-six month context; 2500 lb wagon capacity; supplies and finite purchases mattered.
sources.limits: Do not equate total outfit and first-year support cost with remaining cash or use its 1849 Ware list as an exact 1848 list.

sources.supports: April/May timing, winter pass risk, declining late-route game and harder western terrain; Barlow Road from 1846.
sources.limits: No exact monthly weather table, hunting success probability or population victory rate.

sources.supports: Construction began June 1848; early travelers passed before construction; initially scant buildings and supplies.
sources.limits: Does not establish the quantity or price of a particular 1848 shop or medical service.

sources.date: Gold Rush years; Winslow death June 8, 1849
sources.supports: Major trail epidemic belongs to the later Gold Rush context.
sources.limits: Not proof of zero infection in all 1848 places, or of game disease frequencies.

sources.supports: Four-six oxen as a common outfit; differing stock/tack prices and typical supplies.
sources.limits: Wide dates and places; its mule prices differ sharply from current $50. Do not silently substitute one aggregate list for a dated local transaction.

sources.supports: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy; storage and heat can reduce vitamin C.
sources.limits: Does not validate one shared deficiency counter, exact game drying retention or preserved fruit as a guaranteed prevention method.

sources.date: Designer retrospective on 1985 design and later adaptations
sources.supports: 100 lb hunting haul was a game design decision; regional ecology and shooting skill were deliberate mechanics.
sources.limits: Classic rules are design references, not historical measurements; do not copy a haul cap as physiological evidence.
